title: Grateful Dead Live at Various on 1966-03-12
source: Acid Test material, labelled with numbers 5,6 in supplement to previous 4 disc set.

ai_review.summary: A historically rich soundboard capture of the 1966 Acid Test set with tight, blues‑heavy performances and generally good audio despite some noise.
ai_review.review: The supplement presents an early‑era Dead show that feels soulful and high‑energy, highlighted by a rousing Viola Lee Blues, a fiery Next Time You See Me, and Jerry’s surprising licks in In the Midnight Hour.  The soundboard source is reasonably clear—tight and listenable—though a few reviewers note occasional background hiss or “garbage” noise.  Overall the recording is prized for its historical value as much as its musical punch.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give five‑star ratings and praise both the performance and historic significance; recording quality is described as tight but with some noise, yielding a solid combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally tight mix and clear enough for listening; a few mentions of background hiss/garbage noise but no major dropouts or balance issues.

standout_songs: Beat It On Down The Line (BIODTL)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early blues‑heavy set that flows through traditional numbers and jam sections; the band moves from acoustic roots to electrified jams with a cohesive, soulful vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Noted for surprising lead licks in In The Midnight Hour and strong vocal on It's A Sin; praised for his early‑era playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned having choppier bass notes than later versions, still enjoying the groove.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s vocals highlighted on Beat It On Down The Line (BIODTL) and contribution to the blues feel.
